items.title: Fix ./ros hitting an unhandled 404 for a main-branch snapshot rosVersion
items.description: A project bootstrapped via the documented @main install flow gets a ros.json rosVersion like 2.0.1-main.78.1; publish.yml never builds/publishes a binary for snapshot versions, so the launcher's blind download attempt surfaced a raw 404 instead of a clear error.

items.title: Fix ros-bootstrap init pinning a scaffolded project to a binary-less @main snapshot version
items.description: Bootstrapping via the documented @main install flow writes a ros.json rosVersion (e.g. 2.0.1-main.78.1) that never has a matching GitHub Release, so ./ros can never run -- the earlier launcher fix (WI-0053) only made the failure message clearer. Fixed by pinning ros.json to the newest stable release with real binaries instead, via a version bundled into the npm tarball at publish time (DF-ROS-2026-A034).

items.title: Sync queue.json's own backlog status to complete when a promoted item finishes
items.description: The backlog triage lifecycle has no complete transition (ready|block|abandon only), so a promoted-then-completed item's raw queue.json status stayed frozen forever, only ever looking correct in queue.md's merged rendering after some later, unrelated backlog write. Fixed at the source: FileBacklogQueueRepository.markComplete, wired into work complete.

items.title: Stop work complete from sweeping ROS_BASE_REF committed-range paths into its completion event
items.description: With ROS_BASE_REF set, work complete includes committed-range paths (possibly from before the work item began) in its work.completed paths, recording them as contemporaneous attribution. Post-hoc changes should go through work reconcile instead. Changing this diverges from the frozen Node golden masters (work-complete differential), so it needs a decision. Follow-up from GH-80 / DF-ROS-2026-A040.

items.title: Content-match symbolic links and submodules for reconciled attribution
items.description: ReconciliationCoverage hashes working-tree content with git hash-object, which follows symlinks and cannot hash submodules, so a reconciled symlink or submodule path never matches its recorded blob and always fails validation (fail closed). Compare the link target text / gitlink commit instead. Follow-up from GH-80 / DF-ROS-2026-A040.

items.title: ActorKind extension pattern accepts a trailing newline ($ anchor)
items.description: ActorKind.tryParse (src/Ros.Domain/Provenance/Actor.fs) matches ^x-[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$ with a .NET $ anchor, which also matches before a trailing newline, so 'x-agent\n' parses as an extension kind. Fix: anchor with \z and add a test; audit other Domain patterns for the same anchor.

items.title: Adapter recognizes GitHub rate limiting on push and pull-request creation (PRX-REMOTE-038)
items.description: Child of GH-90. RQ-ROS-2026-A021 1.1.0 records the remaining PRX-REMOTE-038 gap: scripts/praxis-remote-persist.sh reports any non-conflict push failure, and any pull-request creation failure, as repository-write-failed, although the protocol already defines rate-limited. Classify GitHub rate limiting (HTTP 429, primary/secondary API rate limit) as rate-limited with same-request retry, keep concurrency-conflict and other write failures distinct, and test against real Git remotes. Depends on: PRAXIS-REMOTE-06.

items.title: Pull-request persistence: a same-request retry after the state branch was pushed is misreported as concurrency-conflict
items.description: Found in PRAXIS-REMOTE-13. In persistence: pull-request mode, scripts/praxis-remote-persist.sh pushes praxis/remote/<digest(requestId)> before gh pr create. If PR creation then fails (rate-limited or repository-write-failed, both advising same-request retry), the retry runs on a fresh checkout, produces a different commit, and pushing it to the existing per-request branch is non-fast-forward, so the adapter reports concurrency-conflict/after-refresh, contradicting the same-request advice. Decide how a retry recognizes and reuses its own existing state branch (e.g. open the PR for it) without force-pushing.
items.abandonedReason: Allocated by 'ros add' with an ID that collides with the completed work item WI-0061 in the live context (generated IDs are checked against the queue only). The obligation is re-captured as PRAXIS-REMOTE-14; the allocator defect as WORK-CAPTURE-ID-COLLISION.

If PR creation then fails (rate-limited or repository-write-failed, both advising same-request retry), the retry runs on a fresh checkout, produces a different commit, and pushing it to the existing per-request branch is non-fast-forward, so the adapter reports concurrency-conflict/after-refresh, contradicting the same-request advice. items.title: queue.md shows the pre-promotion backlog status after work start/complete until the next backlog write

Readers of the human projection (and agents) can mistake in-flight work for ready work. Fix: regenerate queue.md from QueuePresentation.mergedRows on every live transition that changes effective status (start/block/resume/complete/abandon), with a test. Evidence: research/experiments/EX-ROS-2026-A022-target-gate/signal/gh5-state-investigation.txt.
